target_only_tests.why: Seven cases, none counted as ported coverage, all six added by continuo#92 and required by D-0047. A mismatched identity has two legitimate detection points -- the readout the provider takes immediately after the spawn, which the verb then answers with, and the read-back poll `#awaitIdentity` runs afterwards -- and with a real child which of them fires first is event-loop scheduling against process startup. interlock's suite has no case for either forced path; its `test_a_reported_identity_that_disagrees_is_never_confirmed` asserts one refusal class and gets whichever path the machine happened to run, which is how a continuo pull request touching no code went red on a contended Windows runner. The first four force one detection point each, across both verbs that share `#spawn` (`start` and `resume`), and assert the caller-visible class does not move. The fifth covers a third detection point that only a provider which does not persist its incidents can reach: `recover` probes `readState` before it resumes, and a walk that resumed on the strength of having asked too early would bury the incident under a new generation (found by the Codex review of this change). The sixth is the regression guard that the redirect is not over-broad: a `Failure` whose `detail` says `identity incident` but whose kind is `UNINTERPRETABLE_RESPONSE` is still `ProviderStartFailed`, which is what makes the discriminator a kind rather than a string match. The seventh pins the ordering the new path must not bypass -- the fenced post-spawn gate runs before the identity refusal is raised, so a claimant that lost its lease leaves as `LoserTerminated` with its child handled. Five further cases, added by continuo#174 and required by D-0098, cover the post-spawn read-back WINDOW rather than what is read back in it. The source bounds the poll with a hard-coded 50 attempts at 50 ms and interlock has no case for the size of that window at all -- correctly, because in-memory it is never met: a scripted provider answers on the first ask. Against a real `claude` it is never met the other way, which is what rondo's lap-1 dogfood measured (3.55 s cold, 7.9-11.3 s warm to the first event, against a 2.5 s window), so every lap on a real CLI ended at `readback-exhausted` with the binding left at 'spawned'. The first case pins that a caller's budget buys the polls it pays for and that the refusal quotes the caller's own number, which is what lets an operator tell 'the window I set ran out' from 'a constant I cannot reach ran out'. The second pins the rounding at the bottom, where truncation would refuse a provider that had already answered. The third pins the default itself -- thirty seconds, above the slowest measurement -- because a default that clears one measurement and not the next is the same defect in a smaller size. The fourth keeps a mistyped budget a caller's defect (`RangeError`) rather than a silent zero-poll walk. The fifth is the anti-vacuity half and the one that would fail a fix of the wrong shape: a readout that NAMES the committed identity but reports the child's own exit is still refused however large the budget is, so widening the window cannot be mistaken for loosening `defaultIdentityConfirmation`.

systematic_mappings.from: `SessionOrchestrator.start()` / `.recover()` are ordinary blocking Python calls; the five `SessionProvider` verbs they drive are synchronous in the source.
systematic_mappings.to: `SessionOrchestrator.start()` / `.recover()` are `async` and every call site in this file `await's them.
systematic_mappings.why: D-0301 made continuo's `SessionProvider` verbs `Promise`-returning (Node has no synchronous way to wait for a child to exit), so `src/supervisor.ts` (D-0801) is `async` end to end. This is a calling-convention change with no effect on what any case asserts -- every value compared, every row read, every exception type is the source's -- so it is recorded once here rather than argued per case, and no case is marked `adapted` for it alone (consistent with how the session belt's own ledgers treat the same D-0301 change).

systematic_mappings.to: `expectAsyncRefusal(() => promise, SomeError, match)`, this belt's local async twin of `test/testkit/errors.ts`'s `expectRefusal` (kept local to `test/gate_item2/helpers.ts` rather than added to the shared testkit while other belts are mid-flight against it).
systematic_mappings.why: Same reason as above: the refusal now arrives as a rejected promise. Both halves `pytest.raises` checks -- the exception class and a `match` search over its string form -- are kept.
systematic_mappings.affects: every case that expects a refusal

entries.reason: The source's session_uuid_factory raises KeyboardInterrupt to simulate the claimant dying inside the admission window and asserts `pytest.raises(KeyboardInterrupt)`. TypeScript has no analogue of KeyboardInterrupt as a distinguished exception type reachable from user code, so the seam raises a plain Error and the assertion checks the message text via `.rejects.toThrow(<message>)` instead of a class. Every other assertion in the case -- zero start calls, zero active rows before the retry, LeaseHeld on the too-early retry, the eventual single spawn under the retry's own identity -- is carried unchanged.

entries.reason: The source restores the patched `provider.read_state` with `del provider.read_state`, which removes the instance attribute and lets attribute lookup fall through to the class's bound method -- Python's normal instance/class shadowing. TypeScript's `ScriptedProvider.readState` is a prototype method with no distinguished 'delete the instance override' operation with the same effect available at the call site used here, so the port captures the original bound method and reassigns it back explicitly (`provider.readState = originalReadState`) inside the patched function, before calling through to it. The effect on the provider's dispatch is identical -- the second attempt sees the original implementation -- and every assertion (StaleWriterRefused, zero resume calls, a durable post_spawn_gate refusal, the binding's session id unchanged) is carried unchanged.
